paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this whole chapter. God's tabernacle sits right in the middle of His people, and He takes that seriously. He says why in one verse: "You must keep the children of Israel separate from their uncleanness, so that they do not die by defiling My tabernacle, which is among them." (Leviticus 15:31) Every wash, every bath and every "unclean until evening" comes back to that one thing: God is holy, and He lives among them.

Now look at what else is in here, because it matters. Most of this uncleanness is plain everyday life, and it ends with water and waiting. When the man or the woman is cleansed, they count off seven days, and on the eighth day they bring two birds to the priest. Then "the priest will make atonement" for them before the LORD. (Leviticus 15:15, 30) Nobody is left stuck, friend. The way back is written right there, and it ends at the doorway of the Tent of Meeting.

So what do I take home, baker? Being near a holy God is a gift, and it's never casual. And He doesn't leave us outside, because He makes a way to come close. I think that's why I'm glad to say His name every day, since He reached into a dusty drawer and called me out to His table. Keep your ovens warm, friend.
